topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and sets the learning outcomes for evaluating cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetics, Endogenous Processes, and Environmental Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental mechanisms of cancer development, debating the relative roles of endogenous errors ('bad luck'), inherited predisposition, and environmental exposures supported by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens drive carcinogenesis, featuring an overview of viral and bacterial mechanisms and a detailed case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Activation, Adducts, and DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how chemical and physical agents—including dietary aflatoxins, UV radiation, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and aromatic amines—undergo xenobiotic metabolism to directly damage DNA.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish cancer initiators from promoters, describing how chronic inflammation, intracellular signaling, and host developmental stages create permissive conditions for tumor growth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity and Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their carcinogenic potency and risk.
